Round LXXIX (audit #56): can this filename possibly be read, judging by the extension alone?

Source: R/agent_ingest.R
cv_upload_extension_problem.Rd

Returns `NULL` when the upload should proceed, or `list(message=, detail=)` when it should not.

Usage

cv_upload_extension_problem(filename)

Arguments

filename

the name the browser sent.

Details

WHY IT RUNS BEFORE THE BYTES ARE STAGED. `cv_api_upload_multipart()` writes a full second copy of the payload to `tempfile()` and only then hands it to the reader. On a `.h5ad` – the single most likely wrong format for this audience, since it is what a Scanpy user has – every byte was written, read and thrown away to produce a message the FILENAME already determined.

THERE IS NO SIZE LIMIT HERE AND MUST NOT BE ONE. The audit pairs this item with "state an upload size limit"; that half is refused under the project's standing no-upload-limits policy, and refusing it is a decision rather than an oversight. A biologist with a 40 GB atlas is the user this tool is for.

An empty extension is ACCEPTED, not refused. A programmatic caller can post bytes under a form-field name with no extension at all, and `cv_api_upload_multipart()` has always defaulted that to `.rds`; turning a working path into an error would be a regression dressed as a guard.
